description: Make the frozen-comparand oracle-lint rule quote-aware (strip quoted spans, unwrap -c wrapper payloads) so comparison-shaped text sitting inside quoted data stops being misread as a live shell comparison.

userStories.title: Review round 1 fix 001: address reviewer finding
userStories.notes: CRITICAL [src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts:200]: stripQuotedSpans resolves the closing quote with indexOf and, on no match (closeIdx === -1), sets end = command.length, swallowing the rest of the command; it also has no handling for the POSIX single-quote-escape idiom ('\''). Result: a genuine live comparison that main correctly FLAGGED is now silently excused. Verified by reviewer against main's reconstructed pre-fix predicate: "sh -c 'echo '\''hi'\''; test $(wc -l < f) -eq 3'" -> main=FLAG, branch=ok; "printf '%s' a'b; test $(wc -l < f) -eq 7" -> main=FLAG, branch=ok. That escape idiom is valid, common shell, so this is a real false-negative regression in the rule's core detection duty, and it lands squarely in the CAM-383 over-excusing class the PRD notes explicitly forbid trading into ('otherwise you trade over-flagging for CAM-383's over-excusing'). No fixture row covers an escaped or unbalanced quote. Fix: treat an unterminated quote as literal text rather than consuming to end-of-string, and handle the '\'' escape; add a fixture row for each shape.

userStories.title: Review round 1 fix 002: address reviewer finding
userStories.notes: WARNING [src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts:176]: isDashCWrapper matches ANY '-c' flag token preceding a quote (/(?:^|\s)-c\s*$/), not an interpreter's -c as its own docstring states ('e.g. sh -c '...', bash -c "..."', :169-170). A non-interpreter -c payload is therefore unwrapped and scanned as live shell: "grep -c 'test $X -eq 41' file.ts" and "npx tool -c 'threshold -eq 5'" both FLAG on the branch even though their only operator+integer byte pattern is inert quoted data. Not a regression (main flags them too), but an uncorrected instance of exactly the false-positive class this story exists to close, and 'grep -c' is a first-class idiom in this very module (GREP_COUNT_GUARD_RE at :346 matches 'grep -c ... -ge N'). Fix: scope the unwrap to a preceding shell-interpreter word (sh/bash/zsh/dash), and add a 'grep -c' ok row to the fixture matrix.

userStories.title: Make frozen-comparand quote-aware with -c payload unwrapping
userStories.description: As a plan author, I need the frozen-comparand rule to ignore operator+integer byte patterns that sit inside quoted spans (while still recursing into `-c '<payload>'` wrappers) so that behavioral oracles about the rule itself, and ordinary grep-search-pattern oracles, stop being false-positived and burning entire planning cycles.
acceptanceCriteria: RED ON MAIN, measured exhaustively (3/3 wrongly flagged against unmodified main on 2026-07-20): the three verbatim oracle commands from the real CAM-382 false-positive incident are stored in a tracked, durable fixture at test/fixtures/oracle-lint/cam382-false-positives.txt (one command per line, '#' comments allowed) and every one of them classifies ok under the fixed rule; the guard rejects a narrowed incident set. PINNING CRITERION, classification component deliberately GREEN on main, falsifiable only against a regression that routes the rotating rule through the new stripper: the fixture carries at least one rotating-artifact-target `flag` row whose rotating path sits inside quotes, and it still flags, preserving that rule's documented intentional quote-blindness (src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts:209-211). userStories.notes: Files: src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts (hasFrozenIntegerComparand at :164-171, plus a new module-local stripper), test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts, and two NEW tracked fixtures under test/fixtures/oracle-lint/: cam382-false-positives.txt (the three verbatim incident commands, one per line) and oracle-lint-cases.txt (the `<rule> :: <ok|flag> :: <command>` matrix). SOURCING THE INCIDENT COMMANDS: extract them ONCE from .claude/.cam-plan-escalated.json and commit them into the tracked fixture. That marker is gitignored (.gitignore:87), untracked, rotating, and is DESTROYED by this plan's own outcome (src/commands/sidecar.ts:2319 wires removeEscalationMarkerFn; src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts:1376-1383 removes it on any converging audit-approved path, ungated on issueId). Never read it from an acceptance oracle: that is exactly the never-target-a-rotating-artifact rule at patterns.md:907. If the marker is already gone when you start, the three commands are reproduced verbatim in this issue's description body (scripts/cam/issues/CAM-0388.json) and in the CAM-382 escalation narrative. SEED ROWS for oracle-lint-cases.txt (US-002 broadens the matrix): a quoted-JS-payload case expected ok, a `grep -qF '<search pattern containing a comparison>' <file>` case expected ok, a bare live comparison expected flag, a `sh -c '<live comparison>'` wrapper expected flag, and a rotating-artifact-target case whose path is quoted expected flag. DESIGN (fixed by the issue spec, do not re-litigate): strip single/double-quoted spans before scanning, but UNWRAP (recurse into) `-c '<payload>'` wrapper payloads rather than deleting them. Strip ONCE and run BOTH INTEGER_COMPARAND_RE and LIVE_DERIVATION_RE against the same stripped text, otherwise you trade over-flagging for CAM-383's over-excusing. DO NOT TOUCH (each is a separate specified issue): the missing LEFT word boundary on INTEGER_COMPARAND_RE (CAM-382), the operator alternation widening (CAM-382), LIVE_DERIVATION_RE's \bmain\b (CAM-386), the over-excusing behavior (CAM-383), and ROTATING_ARTIFACT_RULE (its quote-blindness is intentional and documented at :209-211 with a test at :266). PURITY: the module is pure with exactly two imports and declares 'Pure, no I/O' at :30-31 (journal.md:517 records CAM-381 preserving it). The fixtures are read by the TEST and by the acceptance oracles, never by the lint module. COMPLEXITY: biome enforces cognitive complexity; extract the stripper as its own named module-local function rather than inlining it into hasFrozenIntegerComparand. SELF-REFERENTIAL TRAP: this rule classifies shell comparisons, so operator+integer literals live in the FIXTURES, never inlined into an acceptance-oracle command. Do not obfuscate operator literals via string concatenation to dodge the lint; if a needed oracle cannot be authored without tripping the unfixed rule, HALT and report. Patterns to grep before coding: patterns.md:899 (red-on-main falsifiability), :901 (zero-match-vacuous), :903 (derive-don't-freeze), :907 (never-target-a-rotating-artifact). NEEDS REBUILD after merge: prd-oracle-lint.ts is sidecar-executed at plan time, so the fix has no effect until the binary is rebuilt and the sidecar respawned.

userStories.title: Broaden the fixture matrix and record the accepted detection trade-off
userStories.description: As a future maintainer of this rule, I need the behavioral fixture to be non-vacuous in both directions and the accepted blind spot to be written down, so a later story cannot narrow the fixture into vacuity and nobody re-discovers the -e-payload hole by accident.
acceptanceCriteria: FIXTURE-SHAPE GUARD, green the moment the broadened matrix exists (its job is to stop the fixture from being narrowed into vacuity), red on main today: the frozen-comparand rows cover all four required shapes, at least one each of a quoted test-input payload expected ok, a grep search pattern expected ok, a bare live comparison expected flag, and a -c wrapper payload expected flag. RED ON MAIN, re-run over the broadened matrix (this is the criterion the new rows must actually satisfy, not a re-statement of US-001's seed check): every row of test/fixtures/oracle-lint/oracle-lint-cases.txt still classifies as its recorded expectation after the matrix is broadened. RED ON MAIN (neither phrase exists on main): the accepted detection trade-off is recorded as a durable bullet in scripts/cam/patterns.md, stating that quote-stripping intentionally blinds frozen-comparand to comparisons embedded in non-`-c` interpreter payloads (notably `bun -e '...'`, the shape of two of the three replayed CAM-382 commands), and that `-c` is unwrapped while `-e` is not.
